blocks.text: The direction of electron flow in the wires of the external circuit is deduced by comparing the E standard values of the two half-cells. In Figure 10.9 the voltages are Ag+(aq) + e- giving Ag(s), +0.80 V, and Zn2+(aq) + 2e- giving Zn(s), -0.76 V. The relative values show that Zn2+ ions are more difficult to reduce than Ag+ ions, so zinc metal loses electrons to the Ag+/Ag half-cell and Ag+ ions accept electrons from the Zn2+/Zn half-cell. The electrons move through the wires in the external circuit, not through the electrolyte solution: the flow is from the Zn2+/Zn half-cell to the Ag+/Ag half-cell, from the negative pole to the positive pole, since the more positive pole attracts the negative electrons.
